Fact.Name: Schedule 3 is attached to the return
Fact.Description: TRUE when the return attaches Schedule 3 (Form 1040). The schedule carries two figures to Form 1040: line 8, the Part I nonrefundable credits, to Form 1040 line 20, and line 15, the Part II other payments and refundable credits, to Form 1040 line 31. It is attached whenever either one is more than zero (/line8OfSchedule3, /otherPaymentsAndRefundableCreditsTotal), each read only once it is complete. The four single-credit tests (the saver's credit, the credit for the elderly or the disabled, the child and dependent care credit, and a net premium tax credit) are kept beside the two totals, so a return that attached the schedule through one of them still does.

Fact.Name: Schedule 3 line 1 (foreign tax credit)
Fact.Description:
Schedule 3 Line 1: foreign tax credit → line 8 → 1040 line 20. TWO SOURCES, and the printed forms name both: a return on the no-Form-1116 exception carries foreignTaxCredit /foreignTaxCreditAmount, and a return that files Form 1116 carries form1116 /form1116Line35ForeignTaxCredit, because line 35 is printed "Subtract line 34 from line 33. This is your foreign tax credit. Enter here and on Schedule 3 (Form 1040), line 1".
THIS FACT ROUTES THROUGH foreignTaxCredit:/foreignTaxCreditWithSection904Limitation. It used to be a bare alias of /foreignTaxCreditAmount, so the 135 facts form1116.xml ships computed a section 904 limited credit that reached nothing: Form 1116 line 35 printed and Form 1040 line 20 never saw it. That was the under-credit half of the same defect /knockoutForeignTaxRequiresForm1116 exists to prevent, held off the wire only by the knockout itself.
THE ARMS ARE ORDERED, AND THE ORDER IS THE POINT. (1) foreignTaxCredit /qualifiesForNoForm1116Exception TRUE → /foreignTaxCreditAmount, exactly today's value. The exception is an ELECTION not to file Form 1116 (the Form 1116 instructions: "You may be able to claim the foreign tax credit without filing Form 1116"), so a filer who qualifies for it keeps the amount this line has always carried, and no return that qualifies can have its value moved by anything Form 1116 computes. (2) otherwise, form1116 /form1116Answered TRUE → /form1116Line35ForeignTaxCredit. That predicate is answered-ness on the RAW /form1116ForeignCountries collection intake, not IsComplete on a complete-safe line — see its Description. (3) otherwise → /foreignTaxCreditAmount, which is a complete-safe $0 on every return that neither qualifies for the exception nor opened Form 1116. This is the fallback arm, and it is why the line stays Complete on a return that never answers a foreign-tax intake.
ARM 2 IS DELIBERATELY NOT COMPLETE-SAFE. /form1116Line35ForeignTaxCredit goes Incomplete on a half-answered Form 1116 (line 22 and line 34 are filer entries, and line 10 is Incomplete on a return with no Schedule B until the attestation is answered), and wrapping it in an OrZero would file a $0 foreign tax credit for a filer who has begun the form — a silent under-credit, the exact class this rewire closes. An unfinished Form 1116 leaves the line unresolved and the return unfileable, which is the honest state.
THE KNOCKOUT STAYS. foreignTaxCredit /knockoutForeignTaxRequiresForm1116 still blocks every return that claims foreign tax and fails the exception — i.e. the whole population arm 2 serves — so this rewire changes no FILED return today. Narrowing or retiring that knockout is separate work.
BYTE-IDENTICAL. No committed scenario answers /form1116ForeignCountries (grep of scenarios/ finds no "form1116" at all, and no interview screen creates the collection), so arm 2 is unreachable corpus-wide and every scenario keeps the value arm 1 or arm 3 gives it — the same /foreignTaxCreditAmount it read before.

Fact.Description:

Fact.Name: Schedule 3 line 6l (Form 8978 line 14)
Fact.Description:

Line 1 is Form 1040 line 18 (taxCalculations /totalTentativeTax); line 2 is /sched3Line6lWorksheetLine2NegativeForm8978Amount, the negative Form 8978 line 14 as a positive number; line 3 enters the lesser of the two here, floored at $0.
A POSITIVE Form 8978 line 14 never reaches this line: "If the amount on Form 8978, line 14, is positive, see the instructions for Form 1040 or 1040-SR, line 16", where it is additional tax (taxCalculations /otherFormForm8978Tax). So this line is never negative.

Otherwise it takes line 2's completeness, so an entered Form 8978 whose line 14 is not yet complete leaves this line Incomplete, and a return that enters no Form 8978 carries a Complete $0.

The derivation is on form6251:/knockoutAmtUnmodeledPreference's own Description; the Form 8801 section header in dictionary/ty2025/form6251.xml records the two-commit landing.

Schedule 3 line 7 WITHOUT its line-6b term — the SEVEN line-6a-through-6z credits this dictionary models other than the prior year minimum tax credit (elderlyAndDisabled /totalEdc at 6d, /sched3Line6c, /sched3Line6f, /sched3Line6g, /sched3Line6l, /sched3Line6m, /sched3Line6h). This fact started as the VERBATIM former body of /totalOtherNonrefundableCredits, split out rather than rewritten.
WHY IT EXISTS: Form 8801 line 22 subtracts "Schedule 3 (Form 1040), lines 1 through 6z (not including any credit for prior year minimum tax on line 6b)", so the 6b-free subtotal /sched3CreditsThrough6zExcluding6b below needs a 6b-free line-7 term to sum. Building that subtotal out of /totalOtherNonrefundableCredits instead would close the dependency loop 6b → line 7 → 8801 line 22 → line 24 → line 25 → 6b: the values cancel, the EDGE does not, and the Fact Graph resolves on edges.
VALUE-IDENTICAL BY CONSTRUCTION AT THE SPLIT: the six addends and their order were unchanged and no Round was introduced, so /totalOtherNonrefundableCredits = this + 6b is exactly the old sum wherever 6b is zero — which is every committed scenario. THE 6h ADDEND IS ALSO VALUE-NEUTRAL on every committed scenario, for a different reason: it is complete-safe 0 unless the Form 8859 carryforward is answered, and no committed scenario answers it.

"Schedule 3 (Form 1040), lines 1 through 6z (not including any credit for prior year minimum tax on line 6b)" — the subtrahend Form 8801 line 22 names, and the ONLY consumer of this fact. It is /line8OfSchedule3's own term list with /totalOtherNonrefundableCredits replaced by its 6b-free half: lines 1, 2, 3, 4, 5a, 5b plus /otherNonrefundableCreditsExcluding6b.
NOT A SUBSTITUTE FOR /line8OfSchedule3, which keeps its printed shape (lines 1 through 4, 5a, 5b and line 7, 6b included) and needed no edit. Routing 8801 line 22 through this fact rather than through line 8 is what keeps the graph acyclic; see /otherNonrefundableCreditsExcluding6b.
LINE 6k (Form 8912, credit to holders of tax credit bonds) IS EXCLUDED HERE AND ONLY HERE. The Form 8801 line 22 instruction names TWO exclusions, not one: "Schedule 3 (Form 1040), lines 1 through 6z (not including any credit for prior year minimum tax on line 6b or any credit claimed on Form 8912 ...)" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-pdf/i8801.pdf, page 4). The line 6b exclusion is carried by reading /otherNonrefundableCreditsExcluding6b instead of /totalOtherNonrefundableCredits; the Form 8912 exclusion is expressed as an omission from this fact's own addend list rather than a subtraction — see below for why. Without excluding it, this fact would be HIGH by the Form 8912 credit, making Form 8801 line 22 LOW, line 24 LOW and the prior year minimum tax credit UNDER allowed for a filer who holds both a tax credit bond credit and an AMT carryforward. Complete-safe 0 wherever line 6k is unanswered, which is every committed scenario, so nothing moved.
LINE 6h (Form 8859, DC first-time homebuyer) IS PRESENT IN BOTH: dictionary/ty2025/form8859.xml exists, and 6h is summed by /otherNonrefundableCreditsExcluding6b, which this fact sums in turn, so the Form 8801 line-22 treatment of 6h follows automatically from that fact rather than needing its own separate wiring here. Complete-safe 0 wherever the carryforward is unanswered, which is every committed scenario, so nothing moved.
THE 6k EXCLUSION IS AN OMISSION, NOT A SUBTRACTION. Form 8912 computes its own credit against a limitation that reads the return's other Schedule 3 credits, so reading /otherNonrefundableCreditsExcluding6b here and subtracting /sched3Line6k back out would leave the EDGE to line 6k in place and close a dependency loop through that limitation — the values would cancel, the edge would not, and the Fact Graph resolves on edges. The body therefore lists the addends explicitly and simply never names 6k: lines 1, 2, 3, 4, 5a and 5b, plus the same twelve line-6 terms /otherNonrefundableCreditsExcluding6b sums, less /sched3Line6k. Term for term that is the identical value the Subtract produced.

Schedule 3 Line 7: The total of the other nonrefundable credits, including the line-6g term (/sched3Line6g — mortgage interest credit, Form 8396 line 9) and the line-6c term (/sched3Line6c — adoption credit, Form 8839 line 18), both complete-safe 0.
THIS FACT IS SPLIT INTO TWO HALVES: the credits /otherNonrefundableCreditsExcluding6b already carries, PLUS /sched3Line6b (Form 8801 line 25). Line 7 must keep including 6b — that is what Schedule 3 prints — and the split exists so that Form 8801 line 22 can subtract a 6b-FREE subtotal without closing a dependency cycle. VALUE-IDENTICAL on every committed scenario: the addends /otherNonrefundableCreditsExcluding6b carries are unmoved and unreordered, no Round is introduced (exact arithmetic, so the re-association is the same number), and /sched3Line6b resolves Complete 0.00 corpus-wide.
COMPLETENESS IS UNCHANGED TOO, AND THAT HALF IS MEASURED RATHER THAN ARGUED, because a reshape can move a committed row's KIND with its value unmoved. Where it is a Placeholder, the Placeholder is inherited from elderlyAndDisabled:/totalEdc, not from /sched3Line6c, /sched3Line6f, /sched3Line6g, /sched3Line6l or /sched3Line6m. THOSE FOUR CASES ARE THEREFORE THE PROOF, not a worry: the PRE-rebody body ALREADY combined a Placeholder /totalEdc with five Complete siblings and resolved Placeholder, so Add propagates Placeholder out of a mixed-kind operand set on this very fact's committed rows. The post-rebody shape is the same mixed-kind combination one level down (a Placeholder /otherNonrefundableCreditsExcluding6b plus a Complete /sched3Line6b), so those four rows stay Placeholder 0.00 and the other 938 stay Complete. /line8OfSchedule3 tracks it exactly, Placeholder on the same 4.

Fact.Name: Maximum social security tax one employer may withhold for 2025
Fact.Description:
The 2025 annual maximum social security (OASDI) tax for one person, $10,918.20 — the figure Schedule 3 line 11 measures withholding against, and the ceiling the instructions put on any ONE employer's box 4.
DERIVED, NOT A SECOND LITERAL, and that is the point. The W-2 instructions print the identity themselves — "the amount should not exceed $10,918.20 ($176,100 x 6.2%)" — so this fact is 6.2% of the shipping wage base formW2s:/maxOasdiWagesOnMultipleW2sForOnePerson rather than a hardcoded 10918.20. One indexed parameter, two consumers that cannot drift apart: the wage base moves every year with the SSA announcement and this figure moves with it by construction. 176,100 x 0.062 = 10,918.20 exactly, in integer cents.
The 6.2% is the section 3101(a) employee OASDI rate, which is statutory and not indexed, so it is spelled as a Rational rather than ledgered alongside the wage base.

Fact.Name: This W-2's box 4 PLUS its box-14 Tier 1 tax, capped at the per-employer annual maximum
Fact.Description:
One W-2's social security tax withheld (box 4) ADDED to its box-14 Tier 1 RRTA tax, CENTS PRESERVED and capped at /maxOasdiTaxWithheldByOneEmployer — the addend Schedule 3 line 11 sums. The exact twin in shape of formW2s:/formW2s/*/oasdiWagesForKnockoutCalculation, which caps box 3 at the wage base for the same per-person reason.
THE TIER-1 TERM'S PATH NAME UNDER-DESCRIBES THE FACT. It reads "oasdi" and the body is the combined social-security-and-tier-1 pool. The name is kept deliberately rather than corrected: this fact has two consumers (/{primary,secondary}FilerTotalOasdiWithholdingForExcess) and no export, so a rename buys nothing a reader of this paragraph does not already have, while it would delete and re-add a resolved row on every W-2 in the corpus — a churned regression surface for a cosmetic gain. Read the NAME element, not the path.
WHY ONE POOL AND NOT TWO. Line 11 is "Excess social security and tier 1 RRTA tax withheld", and both printed statements of the rule test the two taxes TOGETHER against ONE $10,918.20 ceiling: the Form 1040 instruction says "too much social security or tier 1 railroad retirement (RRTA) tax may have been withheld. You can take a credit on this line for the amount withheld in excess of $10,918.20", and the employer-side statement is even plainer — "had more than $10,918.20 in social security and/or Tier 1 RRTA tax withheld". Neither text gives tier 1 a ceiling of its own. That is why the ADD happens INSIDE the LesserOf: a filer with $6,200 of box 4 from one employer and $6,200 of box-14 Tier 1 from another has $12,400 in the pool and a $1,481.80 credit, where two separate caps would give them nothing. tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-tier1-mixed-fica-and-railroad-one-pool is that filer, and its transcript carries the rejected reading's answer (0.00) beside the computed one.
A RAILROAD EMPLOYER'S BOX 4 IS EMPTY, which is why this term could not have been left to box 4 alone. "Use Form W-2, box 14, to report total RRTA compensation, Tier 1, Tier 2, Medicare ... for each employee covered by RRTA tax", and of boxes 3 through 7: "These boxes are not to be used to report railroad retirement compensation and taxes." So before this term existed, a filer with two railroad employers resolved this fact at $0.00 on both W-2s and Schedule 3 line 11 at $0 — the whole credit lost. That was measured on this branch as the red-first state of tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-tier1-two-railroad-employers, not assumed.
TIER 2 IS EXCLUDED BY PRINTED TEXT AND NOTHING IS BUILT FOR IT: "You can't claim a refund for excess tier 2 RRTA tax on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR. Instead, use Form 843." Its absence from this sum is correct rather than a gap, and tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-tier1-tier2-excluded pins it with a fixture carrying 9,800.00 of Tier 2 that moves line 11 by nothing.
THE CAP IS A FALSE-ALLOWANCE GUARD, not a tidiness measure. The instruction is explicit: "But if any one employer withheld more than $10,918.20, you can't claim the excess on your return. The employer should adjust the tax for you. If the employer doesn't adjust the overcollection, you can file a claim for refund using Form 843." /formW2s/*/writableOasdiWithholding carries no Max limit, so without this cap a single employer's over-collection would flow straight into a refundable credit the filer is told they may not claim. tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-one-employer-over-annual-max pins the divergence: 6,200 claimed against 7,281.80 uncapped.

Fact.Description:
Any W-2 with an affirmative Tier 1 withholding inconsistency, belonging to a filer whose own Schedule 3 line 11 eligibility gate (/{primary,secondary}FilerExceedsMaxOasdiOrTier1Wages — more than one employer AND total wages over $176,100) is answered true. Fact.Name: This W-2's box 3, box 7, and box-14 RRTA compensation, capped at the wage base
Fact.Description:
One W-2's social security wages (box 3), social security tips (box 7), and box-14 RRTA compensation ADDED together, capped at formW2s:/maxOasdiWagesOnMultipleW2sForOnePerson ($176,100) — the per-employer term of the "total wages of more than $176,100" half of the Schedule 3 line 11 eligibility test. Box 7 is in the FICA base because IRC §3121(q) treats tips as remuneration and the W-2 instructions say the wage base is boxes 3 and 7 together. The combined-pool twin of formW2s:/formW2s/*/oasdiWagesForKnockoutCalculation, built to that fact's shape on purpose.
When payroll-confirmed employee Tier 1 taxable compensation is answered, it replaces box-14 RRTA compensation in this measure. The unanswered case retains the original box-14 operand; the confirmed amount and the FICA terms preserve cents through the cap.
WHY THIS EXISTS: THE SHIPPING GATE CANNOT SEE A RAILROAD EMPLOYEE'S WAGES AT ALL. /primaryFilerExcessOasdiWithheld was gated on formW2s:/primaryFilerExceedsMaxOasdiWages, which sums the per-W-2 min(box 3, 176,100). The W-2 instructions say of boxes 3 through 7 that "These boxes are not to be used to report railroad retirement compensation and taxes", so a railroad employee's box 3 is EMPTY by printed rule, that sum reads $0, and the gate is false however much tier-1 tax was withheld. Building the tier-1 withholding term without this one would have left the credit at $0 for exactly the filer it was built for — measured, not assumed: tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-tier1-two-railroad-employers asserts formW2s:/primaryFilerExceedsMaxOasdiWages Complete FALSE beside this gate's true.
THE INSTRUCTION PRINTS ONE TEST, NOT TWO. "If you, or your spouse if filing a joint return, had more than one employer for 2025 and total wages of more than $176,100, too much social security or tier 1 railroad retirement (RRTA) tax may have been withheld." One employer count, one wage threshold, both taxes named on the same line. There is no separate railroad paragraph anywhere in the Line 11 instruction — the sentence above is the whole of it — so the railroad filer's wages belong INSIDE the same measure rather than in a parallel one.
WHY BOX-14 "RRTA COMPENSATION" IS THE WAGE TERM, argued rather than assumed. The W-2 instructions put a railroad employee's compensation there and nowhere else: "Use Form W-2, box 14, to report total RRTA compensation, Tier 1, Tier 2, Medicare (excluding Additional Medicare Tax), and any Additional Medicare Tax withheld ... Label them 'RRTA compensation,' 'Tier 1 tax,' ...". It is the only railroad compensation figure this dictionary holds.
DEFINED HERE, NOT IN formW2s — THE PREMISE IS CORRECTED. At the time this fact was authored, extending formW2s:/formW2s/*/oasdiWagesForKnockoutCalculation was rejected on the belief that it fed a live refusal: /primaryFilerTotalOasdiWagesForKnockout -> /anyFilerExceedsMaxOasdiWages -> imported:/knockoutFormW2s, read then as "a KNOCKOUT". That premise was already false when written — /anyFilerExceedsMaxOasdiWages had already left the return-level refusal aggregator (see formW2s.xml's own retirement note on that chain) and imported:/knockoutFormW2s carries no BlockSubmissionOnTrue and no reader of its own — so the chain this paragraph declined to touch ends at a reader-less aggregator, not a knockout. formW2s:/formW2s/*/oasdiWagesForKnockoutCalculation has since been widened to box 3 + box 7, on exactly the reasoning this fact's own Description makes below (the "THE FICA ARM IS MISSING BOX 7" paragraph); it is now the SHAPE THIS FACT SHOULD COPY when its own box-7 fix (named two paragraphs below) is taken, not a boundary to defer to. formW2s:/primaryFilerExceedsMaxOasdiWages keeps its exact shipping meaning regardless — this fact still owns what line 11 does and still duplicates rather than reuses the upstream chain, because the two measures differ in what they add (RRTA compensation here, nothing there) even once both read box 3 + box 7 on the FICA side.
THE DISCLOSED RESIDUAL OF THE WAGE TERM, stated with its direction. Box-14 "RRTA compensation" is the TOTAL (Medicare-equivalent, uncapped) compensation; the tier-1 OASDI-equivalent base is capped at the same $176,100 but can be SMALLER than total compensation for a filer with pay that is Medicare-taxable but tier-1-exempt. Capping each employer's figure at the wage base makes the two coincide below the cap and saturate above it, so the divergence can only appear where an employer's total compensation is under 176,100 and its tier-1 base is lower still — and it points toward ALLOWING the credit (a filer could clear the wage gate on compensation that the tier-1 base would not reach). Bounded by the withholding side, which is measured not estimated: with each employer's tier-1 tax capped at 10,918.20, a filer whose employers withheld no more than 6.2% of their real tier-1 bases cannot show a positive excess anyway. No separate tier-1 wage base is reported on Form W-2, so closing this needs an intake that does not exist.
THE BOX-7 OMISSION WAS AN ADJUDICATED DEFECT, NOT AN OPEN QUESTION — direction: false DENIAL, taxpayer-adverse. This fact added box 3 and box-14 RRTA compensation and stops there, but the social security wage base the printed $176,100 threshold measures is boxes 3 AND 7: Box 5 says "The wages and tips subject to Medicare tax are the same as those subject to social security tax (boxes 3 and 7)", Box 3 defines itself as the base "but not including social security tips and allocated tips", and the cap is printed on the pair in both the Box 3 and the Box 7 instructions. Box 4 is tax on boxes 3 plus 7 by its own instruction, so this measure compares a withholding total taken over one base against a threshold taken over a smaller one, and a tipped filer can pay past the annual maximum while this term has not reached the base. The full verdict, the printed spans that decide it, the measured flip set (ONE case, TWO rows, zero tax value moving) and the sized successor unit are recorded on /primaryFilerExcessOasdiWithheld under THE ELIGIBILITY MEASURE READS BOXES 3 PLUS 7. The fix is one addend here — box 7, cents preserved, inside the same LesserOf.
BOX 7 IS THE THIRD ADDEND in this existing per-employer measure. The box-7 fixture has $175,000 in boxes 3 plus $2,000 in box 7 across two employers, so the combined $177,000 passes the printed wage threshold and computes the $55.80 excess-withholding credit; the paired no-tip control sits exactly at the threshold and keeps the strict gate closed.
TYPE/SIGN/ROUNDING: Dollar, cents preserved (it feeds a comparison, not a printed line). Complete-safe by construction — formW2s:/formW2s/*/oasdiWages defaults an unanswered box 3 to $0, formW2s:/formW2s/*/oasdiTipsUnrounded defaults an unanswered box 7 to $0, and formW2s:/formW2s/*/rrtaCompensationUnrounded does the same for box 14.

Fact.Description: Sum of /formW2s/*/oasdiAndTier1WagesForExcessEligibility across the PRIMARY filer's W-2s, plus /primaryFilerForm499R2W2PrWagesForExcessEligibility (Form 499R-2/W-2PR boxes 20 and 24, capped per statement). Built on formW2s:/primaryFilerW2s, the shipping Filter, so the per-person cap is respected without new machinery — the same construction /primaryFilerTotalOasdiWithholdingForExcess uses on the withholding side, and the exact combined-pool twin of formW2s:/primaryFilerTotalOasdiWagesForKnockout, which this fact does NOT replace: that one uses the same boxes-3-plus-7 base and keeps feeding the OASDI knockout.

Fact.Name: How many of the PRIMARY filer's W-2s name THIS W-2's employer (box b + box c)
Fact.Description:
A count of the primary filer's W-2s that carry the same EMPLOYER KEY as THIS W-2 — box b (the EIN), box c line 1 (the employer name) and box c line 2, the last matched as equal-if-both-answered or absent-on-both. The per-item half of the employer term, and the only new machinery the "more than one employer" half of the Schedule 3 line 11 eligibility test needs.
THE PATH NAME SAYS "Ein" AND THE KEY IS WIDER THAN THAT, deliberately — the same call /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholdingForExcessCalculation records above. Box c joined box b during this unit, when the Form 2678 agent case below was found; the path is kept because this fact has one consumer and no export, so a rename buys a reader nothing this paragraph does not already give, while it would delete and re-add a resolved row on every W-2 in the corpus. Read the Name element and this sentence, not the path.
WHY IT EXISTS: THE PRINTED TEST COUNTS EMPLOYERS AND THIS SURFACE COUNTED PAYROLL DOCUMENTS. "If you, or your spouse if filing a joint return, had more than one employer for 2025 ..." — the gate read formW2s:/primaryFilerW2sCount, a CollectionSize over /formW2s. Two W-2s from ONE employer (a mid-year payroll-system change, an acquisition, a corrected-and-reissued pair) passed a test they do not satisfy, and with them passed a claim on that one employer's over-collection, which the instruction routes to the employer and to Form 843 instead. Measured, not argued: tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-same-employer-two-w2s-denies is RED against the gate without this term, claiming 1,482 where the printed rule gives 0.
THE IDIOM IS THE ONE /scheduleCs/*/qbiIsDuplicatedAttributionTarget LANDED, and its engine argument carries over unchanged: a member fact of a collection is instantiated ONCE PER ITEM, so its own enclosing item is available to it as a fixed value through "..", while an absolute wildcard path resolves from the root and yields the WHOLE sibling vector (Fact.scala's apply sends an absolute path to root, and applyWildcard maps every member). Count is Expression.Aggregate over that vector. The outer iteration is carried by this fact's per-item instantiation, not by any operator. THIS FACT IS THE EASIER CASE of the two: it compares FIELD VALUES, so it needs none of the CollectionItem-as-a-value machinery that fact had to establish — "../ein" is an ordinary relative dependency.
THE GROUPING KEY IS BOX B *AND* BOX C, AND THE SECOND HALF IS NOT BELT-AND-BRACES. Box b does not identify the employer under a Form 2678 payroll agent: "Each Form W-2 should reflect the EIN of the AGENT in box b", and an agent acting "for two or more employers" who pays one individual on behalf of more than one of them "should file separate Forms W-2 for the affected employee reflecting the wages paid by each employer." Two GENUINE employers, one box b. Grouping on box b alone would have merged them and DENIED a credit that is owed — a NEW false DENIAL manufactured by a unit whose whole purpose is closing a false ALLOWANCE, which is the worse trade in both directions this surface argues about. The same printed passage hands over the discriminator: the agent writes "(Name of agent) / Agent for (name of employer) / Address of agent" into BOX C, so box c LINE 1 is the same on both forms and LINE 2 differs. The key is therefore box b, box c line 1 (formW2s:/formW2s/*/employerName) and box c line 2 (formW2s:/formW2s/*/writableEmployerNameLine2) together. tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-agent-filed-two-employers-one-ein-allows holds that filer's 1,482.
EVERY EXTRA CONJUNCT IS MONOTONE-SAFE, which is why adding two of them needs no separate justification: a longer key makes groups FINER, a finer group makes every count SMALLER, a smaller count makes more rows satisfy "less than the filer's W-2 count", and that pushes /primaryFilerHasMoreThanOneEmployerEin toward TRUE — toward the allowance that was already there. No conjunct in this key can manufacture a denial; the worst any of them can do is fail to close the false allowance on some pair it should have grouped.
LINE 2 IS MATCHED AS "EQUAL IF BOTH ANSWERED, OR ABSENT ON BOTH", and the second branch is what keeps the whole term from being inert. writableEmployerNameLine2 is OPTIONAL — most W-2s leave it blank, and formW2s's own Description points readers at a derived complete-safe sibling that does not exist — so requiring it ANSWERED would empty every group on every ordinary return and the fix would never fire. NEITHER BRANCH CAN LEAK AN Incomplete, but not because both are "made of IsComplete" — branch one also contains an Equal, and an Equal against an unanswered line 2 IS Incomplete. The reason is the SHORT-CIRCUIT: AllOperator tests its head first and returns Complete(false) immediately (All.scala), so when line 2 is unanswered on either side the leading IsComplete collapses branch one before its Equal is ever forced; branch two is IsComplete-only and always Complete; and Any short-circuits on Complete(true). A row that answers line 2 opposite one that does not is NOT grouped, which is again the safe direction.
THE FOUR IsComplete CONJUNCTS ON BOX B AND BOX C LINE 1 ARE LOAD-BEARING, NOT DEFENSIVE, and they are what makes an unanswered box b or employer name cost the filer nothing. /formW2s/*/ein and /formW2s/*/employerName are bare Writables with no Placeholder, so a bare Equal against an unanswered one is Incomplete, and CountOperator returns Result.Incomplete on ANY Incomplete element (Count.scala's `case _ => Result.Incomplete`). That would have carried up through the gate, hit the existing All(IsComplete, value) wrapper on /primaryFilerExcessOasdiWithheld, and silently zeroed the credit for every return still entering its W-2 section — a NEW false DENIAL created by a unit whose whole job is closing a false ALLOWANCE. AllOperator short-circuits on Result.Complete(false) at the head AND at every tail position (All.scala's accumulator matches Complete(false) before it reaches the Incomplete branch), so an IsComplete conjunct that reads false collapses the element to Complete(false) and Count never sees an Incomplete. Each field needs BOTH of its conjuncts — one for MY value being unanswered, one for the sibling's — because either alone leaves the other side's Equal Incomplete. Pinned by tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-unanswered-ein-falls-back-to-row-count.
WHAT AN UNANSWERED KEY FIELD THEREFORE MEANS HERE: "rows I can PROVE share my employer." A row with no box b counts 0 (not even itself), and a row whose box b is answered does not count siblings whose box b is not. Both readings push /primaryFilerHasMoreThanOneEmployerEin toward TRUE, which is exactly the pre-existing behavior — the employer term can only narrow the gate once the EINs are actually known, never on the strength of a blank.
PER FILER, NOT PER RETURN, AND THAT IS NOT A STYLE CHOICE. Sections 3101 and 3201 cap the pool PER PERSON, so two spouses who work for the SAME employer are two separate situations and their W-2s must not be grouped together. The broadcast is over formW2s:/primaryFilerW2s, the shipping Filter, for that reason and for a second one: a MaybeVector of length K meeting one of length N THROWS (MaybeVector.vectorize2's "cannot operate on vectors of different lengths"), so mixing /formW2s/*/ and /primaryFilerW2s/*/ inside one comparison would be a resolution-time crash rather than an Incomplete. The corpus makes the tax point concrete rather than hypothetical: scenarios/upstream/mfj-30k.json and the four scenarios/units/u057/* cases carry two W-2s bearing EIN 00-0878909, one for each spouse. Grouped globally they would read as one employer and lose a credit; grouped per filer they are untouched, and every one of them is unmoved by this unit.
DEFINED IN schedule3.xml RATHER THAN formW2s.xml for the reason /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholdingForExcessCalculation gives above: it is a Schedule 3 line 11 term with no other consumer. formW2s owns box b; this module owns what line 11 does with it.

Fact.Name: How many of the SECONDARY filer's W-2s name THIS W-2's employer (box b + box c)
Fact.Description: Exact twin of /formW2s/*/primaryFilerW2sWithThisEmployerEinCount broadcast over formW2s:/secondaryFilerW2s — see that fact for the printed test, the engine argument, the three-part employer key (box b, box c line 1, box c line 2), its IsComplete conjuncts and the per-filer grouping; all apply here unchanged and the two must stay the same shape. Its note on the path name under-describing the key applies here too. On a non-MFJ return formW2s:/secondaryFilerW2s is empty and this resolves 0, Complete.

Fact.Name: The PRIMARY filer's W-2s name more than one employer
Fact.Description:
TRUE when the primary filer's W-2s do not all come from one employer — the "had more than one employer for 2025" half of the Schedule 3 line 11 eligibility test, measured on the employer KEY (box b plus box c) instead of on the number of payroll documents. The path says "Ein" and the key is wider — see /formW2s/*/primaryFilerW2sWithThisEmployerEinCount, which owns the key and the reason.
THE FORM IS A COUNT, NOT A DIVISION, AND THAT IS THE WHOLE TRICK. The obvious quantity here is the number of DISTINCT employer EINs, and that number is NOT expressible in this engine: distinct-group counting from per-row facts is the sum over rows of 1/(my group size), and per-row group ATTRIBUTION needs an exact division this engine's Dollar cannot do and an ordering it cannot express (the proof is on /primaryFilerHasAtMostOneOverCapEmployer). That sentence is about attribution only, and it must not be read as the wider claim this paragraph used to make by pointing at residual (c): the group-cap build showed that a per-GROUP figure can be recovered WITHOUT attribution, by Maximum under a pigeonhole guard, and the cap half of the surface is built that way. A distinct-EIN COUNT is still not expressible, because a count has no such maximum-shaped escape. The printed test does not ask for that number. It asks a YES/NO, and a yes/no dodges the obstruction entirely: all of a filer's W-2s share one employer if and only if EVERY row's employer-group is the whole set, so "more than one employer" is "SOME row's group is smaller than the set" — Count(group size less than W-2 count) over zero. Every term is a Count over a broadcast, which /scheduleCs/*/qbiIsDuplicatedAttributionTarget already established as resolvable.
THE FOUR CASES IT HAS TO GET RIGHT, all pinned: K=0, no W-2s — Count over an empty collection is 0, so FALSE (and the row-count conjunct beside this one is false too); K=1 — the single row's group is itself, 1 is not less than 1, FALSE; K rows all one EIN — every group is K, none is less than K, FALSE, which is the correction this unit lands; K rows with two or more EINs — every group is a proper subset, so every row counts and the result is TRUE. Unanswered box b makes a group read 0, which is less than any K>=1 and therefore TRUE, preserving the shipping answer exactly — see /formW2s/*/primaryFilerW2sWithThisEmployerEinCount for why that is the right direction.
IT DOES NOT REPLACE THE ROW-COUNT CONJUNCT, IT JOINS IT. /primaryFilerExceedsMaxOasdiOrTier1Wages keeps formW2s:/primaryFilerW2sCount greater than 1 and ANDs this fact onto it. The row-count term is what still denies a one-W-2 filer whose box b is blank, where this fact alone reads TRUE. Together the two are the printed test on the evidence available: more than one form, and no proof the forms share an employer.
A STRICT NARROWING, WHICH IS WHY IT CANNOT CREATE A FALSE DENIAL. This fact is FALSE only where every answered box b on the filer's W-2s is identical, and in that case the filer had one employer by the only test the return can apply. So the gate it joins allows a subset of what it allowed before: no filer who was allowed a credit on genuinely distinct employers loses it. tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-two-employers-one-split-still-allows is that guard — three W-2s, two employers, one of them issuing two forms — and it was GREEN before this fact and stays green after.
TYPE: Boolean. INCOMPLETE in exactly the circumstances the fact it joins is already Incomplete — an absent /formW2s collection makes the Filter, and so this Count, Incomplete — which is why /primaryFilerExcessOasdiWithheld's All(IsComplete, value) wrapper is still exactly as load-bearing as its own comment says. Re-measured against this new operand rather than assumed: tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-w2-section-absent-complete-safe is unchanged and still green.

Fact.Name: The SECONDARY filer's W-2s name more than one employer
Fact.Description: Exact twin of /primaryFilerHasMoreThanOneEmployerEin — see that fact for the printed test, the four boundary cases and the strict-narrowing argument; all apply here unchanged and the two must stay the same shape. On a non-MFJ return formW2s:/secondaryFilerW2s is empty, the Count is 0 and this resolves Complete false.

Fact.Name: What THIS W-2's employer withheld across ALL of the PRIMARY filer's W-2s
Fact.Description:
The sum of /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholdingForExcessCalculation over every one of the primary filer's W-2s that carries THIS W-2's employer key — box b, box c line 1 and box c line 2, exactly the key /formW2s/*/primaryFilerW2sWithThisEmployerEinCount counts. The GROUP total the $10,918.20 ceiling is supposed to bind, which is the half of the printed rule the employer term left open, which the per-row-attribution impossibility finding names.
THE PREDICATE IS THE COUNT FACT'S PREDICATE, OPERATOR FOR OPERATOR, AND THE TWO MUST STAY IN LOCKSTEP. /primaryFilerHasAtMostOneOverCapEmployer below is a PIGEONHOLE on the two together — it compares a group's SIZE, read from the count fact, against the number of rows whose group busts the ceiling, read from this one. If the two predicates ever drift apart they are measuring different groupings and the pigeonhole stops being sound, so an edit to the employer key is an edit to BOTH facts. tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/ excess-oasdi-split-employer-group-cap-exact asserts the count and this sum on the same rows of one fixture for that reason.
WHY THE ALREADY-CAPPED PER-ROW FACT IS A SAFE SUMMAND, which is not obvious and is what lets this fact exist without a second uncapped per-row term. Write c_i = min(w_i, CAP) for the per-row fact and w_i for the raw box-4-plus-tier-1 pool. Then min(sum of c_i, CAP) equals min(sum of w_i, CAP) ALWAYS: if the capped sum already reaches CAP both sides are CAP, and if it does not then no single c_i reached CAP either, so no row was capped and the two sums are the same number. The ceiling is all this surface ever asks of the group total, so summing the capped rows loses nothing — and it keeps /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholdingForExcessCalculation consumed and its resolved value on every W-2 in the corpus untouched.
A ROW WITH NO USABLE EMPLOYER KEY SUMS TO $0, AND THAT IS THE RIGHT ANSWER RATHER THAN A GAP. An unanswered box b makes both IsComplete conjuncts false, so the row matches nothing — not even itself — and this fact is $0. $0 is below the ceiling, so the row's disallowance below is $0 and the row keeps exactly the PER-ROW cap it has today through /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholdingForExcessCalculation. The unanswered-box-b filer is therefore moved by nothing in this unit, which is what tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-unanswered-ein-falls-back-to-row-count still being green means.
BROADCAST OVER THE PRIMARY FILER'S W-2s, so on a SECONDARY filer's W-2 this fact reads whatever the PRIMARY's rows with that key sum to — usually $0, and non-zero only where the two spouses share an employer (scenarios/upstream/mfj-30k.json is that return). The value is meaningless on such a row and is never consumed there: every consumer aggregates over formW2s:/primaryFilerW2s. The shipping count fact has the identical property for the identical reason.
TYPE: Dollar, cents preserved (the summands are the cents-bearing per-row fact; i1040gi page 23 rounds once at line 11, not here). Complete wherever the W-2 collection is.

Fact.Name: What THIS W-2's employer withheld across ALL of the SECONDARY filer's W-2s
Fact.Description: Exact twin of /formW2s/*/primaryFilerThisEmployerWithholdingForExcess broadcast over formW2s:/secondaryFilerW2s — see that fact for the employer key, the lockstep requirement against the count fact, why an already-capped summand is safe, and the unanswered-box-b case; all apply here unchanged and the two must stay the same shape. On a non-MFJ return formW2s:/secondaryFilerW2s is empty and this resolves $0, Complete.

Fact.Name: How much of THIS W-2's employer's withholding the PRIMARY filer may not claim
Fact.Description:
The group total above $10,918.20, floored at zero: what the instruction routes to the employer and to Form 843 instead of to Schedule 3 line 11. "But if any one employer withheld more than $10,918.20, you can't claim the excess on your return."
SAME VALUE ON EVERY MEMBER OF THE GROUP, BY CONSTRUCTION, and that is the fact about it that everything downstream turns on. The input is a group total, so every W-2 in one employer's group reads the same number here, and a filer's rows carry one distinct value per over-collecting employer, repeated group-size times. THIS IS A COUNT, NOT AN ALLOCATION OF MONEY, and that distinction is the whole reason the per-employer group-disallowance construction could be closed without an engine change. Fact.Name: At most ONE of the PRIMARY filer's employers busted the $10,918.20 ceiling
Fact.Description:
TRUE when no more than one of the primary filer's employers over-collected — the condition under which the group disallowance can be computed EXACTLY, with no division and no ordering. It is a PIGEONHOLE on two row counts, and the argument is short enough to state in full.
THE PIGEONHOLE. Let R be /primaryFilerOverCapEmployerW2Count, the number of the filer's W-2s whose employer group busts the ceiling. Every member of an over-cap group is itself over-cap (they share one group total), so R is the SUM of the sizes of the over-cap groups and each over-cap row's own group size n is one of the addends: n is at most R, always. If exactly one group is over, R is that group's size and every over-cap row reads n = R. If TWO OR MORE are over, then for any one of them R is at least n plus the other group's size, which is at least 1, so n is strictly less than R for EVERY over-cap row. So "some over-cap row has n less than R" is TRUE if and only if two or more employers busted the ceiling — an exact characterisation, not an approximation. This fact is the negation, counted over zero in the shape /primaryFilerHasMoreThanOneEmployerEin already established.
THE GROUP SIZE COMES FROM /formW2s/*/primaryFilerW2sWithThisEmployerEinCount AND THE BUST FROM /formW2s/*/primaryFilerThisEmployerDisallowedWithholding, so the pigeonhole is sound only while those two facts group by the SAME key. They do, operator for operator, and both Descriptions say so; an edit to the employer key is an edit to both.
WHY IT MATTERS — the capability argument this whole unit rests on. What Schedule 3 line 11 needs is the sum, ONCE PER EMPLOYER, of that employer's disallowed over-collection. The per-row disallowance is expressible (above) but it repeats group-size times, and no SYMMETRIC per-row function can be summed back to the per-group figure: if a group of n equal rows must contribute a total of E, each row must contribute E/n, which is forced, and this engine's Dollar cannot do that division exactly — Dollar is a BigDecimal fixed at Scale = 2 with HALF_EVEN, Divide(Dollar, Int) rounds through Fractional[Dollar].div, and there is no Dollar-to-Rational node to escape into exact arithmetic with. Breaking the symmetry needs an order on the rows, which the engine does not offer either. WHAT IT DOES OFFER IS Maximum, an Expression.Aggregate exactly as Count and CollectionSum are — and a maximum needs no attribution at all. When at most one group is over the ceiling, every other row's disallowance is $0, so the MAXIMUM over the filer's rows IS that one group's disallowance, exactly, in integer cents, with no division performed anywhere. This fact is the guard that says when that identity holds.
⚠ NO LONGER CONSUMED BY ANYTHING, since the per-employer group-disallowance construction landed. It was built to choose between /primaryFilerEmployerGroupDisallowedWithholding's Maximum branch and its conservative one; that fact is now a single expression valid for any number of over-cap employers, so it asks this question of nobody. The fact is kept, resolving and asserted, for two reasons: retiring it is a REMOVAL under the delta store and would mix removed rows into a unit whose delta is otherwise adjudicable, and the pigeonhole argument it carries is the record of how the one-over-cap case was proved exact before the general answer existed. Retire it in its own unit, or leave it as documentation.
TYPE: Boolean. TRUE on a filer with no W-2s and on every ordinary return, so the guard is not a narrowing of anything — it selects between two ways of computing a disallowance that is $0 in both on such returns.

Fact.Name: Total over-collection the PRIMARY filer may not claim, counted once per employer
Fact.Description:
The sum over the primary filer's EMPLOYERS of each one's disallowed over-collection — the correction /primaryFilerTotalOasdiWithholdingForExcess subtracts so that the $10,918.20 ceiling binds the employer GROUP rather than the W-2 ROW. This is the fact the per-row-attribution impossibility finding named a need for, and this construction supplies it.
ONE EXPRESSION, VALID FOR EVERY CASE. Writing S for the withholding of this filer's over-collecting employers and G for how many DISTINCT employers those are:
disallowance = S - (ceiling x G)
because each over-cap employer's disallowance is its group total less the ceiling, and summing that over the over-cap employers gives exactly the sum of their group totals less one ceiling apiece. No employer over-collected: S is $0 and G is 0, so the answer is $0. One did: S is that group's total and G is 1. Several did: it still holds.
THIS FACT USED TO BE THREE BRANCHES, and the third was a disclosed defect. It used CollectionSum over the per-row disallowance, which counts each employer's figure once per W-2 in its group instead of once, so a filer with two over-collecting employers was over-disallowed and under-credited — a bounded false DENIAL, taken deliberately because every alternative then expressible was a false ALLOWANCE. On the witness fixture it gave 7,954.60 against a printed 10,918.20. All three branches, and the pigeonhole that chose between them, are replaced by the line above.
WHY THE PER-ROW-ATTRIBUTION IMPOSSIBILITY FINDING DOES NOT APPLY HERE. It proved that any per-row function symmetric in the group forces a division, and rejected dividing the group's DISALLOWANCE by its size because Dollar rounds HALF_EVEN at scale 2 and because a per-row money share is a fabricated allocation. Both objections are about dividing MONEY, and this construction divides none: G is a COUNT, assembled in Int as a sum of 1/n over the over-cap rows and carried as a Rational. See /formW2s/*/primaryFilerOverCapEmployerShare.
THE MULTIPLICATION IS EXACT, AND THE ORDER OF OPERATIONS IS WHY. G arrives as an exact integer rational but NOT necessarily in lowest terms — 4/2 for two two-row groups, 6/3 for a two-row and a three-row group. Multiply(Dollar, Rational) computes (dollars x numerator) / denominator, multiplying BEFORE it divides, and since G is an integer its denominator divides its numerator, so the product is an exact number of cents for any equivalent form of G. Had the project owner divided first, this would round. That ordering is load-bearing and is the reason no engine change was needed.
WHY THE SHAPE IS A SUBTRACTION AND NOT A REBUILT SUM. The consumer could have summed min(group total, ceiling) over employers directly, and cannot: that is the per-group attribution the engine has no operator for. Summing the filer's per-ROW capped withholding and subtracting this figure gets to the same number by a route the engine does have, because the total of the group totals IS the total of the rows.
TYPE: Dollar, cents preserved, never negative — floored at $0, which is defensive rather than load-bearing: S is the sum of the group totals of employers each of which EXCEEDS the ceiling, so S is greater than ceiling x G by construction. Fact.Name: Primary filer meets the Schedule 3 line 11 eligibility test (social security OR tier 1)
Fact.Description:
The printed Schedule 3 line 11 eligibility test, term for term: more than one statement (Forms W-2 and Forms 499R-2/W-2PR), AND more than one EMPLOYER (any Form 499R-2/W-2PR is an employer apart from the Forms W-2; with none, the Form W-2 employer test below), AND the capped combined wage total above $176,100 — three conjuncts. Its wage measure sums each employer's box 3 social security wages, box 7 social security tips, and box-14 RRTA compensation before applying the per-employer cap.
IT IS NO LONGER A SUPERSET OF ANYTHING, and the paragraph this replaces claimed it was. IT READ: "The strict superset of formW2s:/primaryFilerExceedsMaxOasdiWages — min(box3 + box14comp, base) is never less than min(box3, base) — so every filer the shipping gate allowed is still allowed, and the only filers this adds are ones with railroad compensation the old measure could not see." That was true of the TIER-1 widening, which only ever added filers. It stopped being true hours later when the employer-EIN conjunct landed: /primaryFilerHasMoreThanOneEmployerEin can be FALSE where the row count is true, so this gate now DENIES filers the shipping gate allowed. That is the entire point of the conjunct — a filer whose two W-2s carry one employer never had "more than one employer" — and tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-same-employer-two-w2s-denies is one such filer moving 1,482 -> 0. THE ACCURATE STATEMENT OF THE RELATION, in the two directions that matter: against formW2s:/primaryFilerExceedsMaxOasdiWages this gate is NEITHER a superset nor a subset — the wage term only ever widens (min(box3 + box7 + box14comp, base) is never less than min(box3 + box7, base)) and the employer term only ever narrows. Against its OWN immediately prior self, the employer conjunct is a pure narrowing, so no filer denied before is allowed now.
SAME SHAPE AS THE FACT IT REPLACES AT THIS CONSUMER, deliberately, INCLUDING ITS COMPLETENESS. Like formW2s:/primaryFilerExceedsMaxOasdiWages it reads a CollectionSize and a CollectionSum over /formW2s, so it is INCOMPLETE on a return whose W-2 section has not been entered. That is exactly why /primaryFilerExcessOasdiWithheld keeps its All(IsComplete, value) wrapper around this fact rather than dropping it: without the wrapper the incompleteness carried into Schedule 3 line 15 and Form 1040 line 31.
THE "MORE THAN ONE EMPLOYER" HALF IS TWO CONJUNCTS, and the paragraph this replaces said the count term "changes no outcome by itself". That was true of the ROW count and false of the printed test it stood in for. It read: "it is half of the printed test. With the per-employer withholding cap in place a single-employer filer can never show more than $10,918.20 and so can never have a positive excess, so the count term changes no outcome by itself." The reasoning holds only when one employer means one W-2 — the per-employer cap is applied per ROW, so a single employer issuing TWO W-2s could show 12,400.00 and a positive excess, which the row count waved through. The gate now also carries /primaryFilerHasMoreThanOneEmployerEin, which is FALSE when every answered box b on the filer's W-2s is the same. Both conjuncts are kept: the row count is what still denies a one-W-2 filer whose box b is blank. See that fact, and residual (c) on /primaryFilerExcessOasdiWithheld for the cap half that this does NOT close.

Fact.Description:
The sum over the PRIMARY filer's EMPLOYERS of min(that employer's box-4-plus-tier-1 withholding, $10,918.20) — the addend Schedule 3 line 11 subtracts the annual maximum from, plus /primaryFilerForm499R2W2PrSocialSecurityTaxForExcess (Form 499R-2/W-2PR box 21, each statement capped at the same maximum). Built on formW2s:/primaryFilerW2s, the shipping Filter, so the per-person section 3101 cap is respected without new machinery.
THE CEILING BINDS THE EMPLOYER, NOT THE FORM. This fact used to be a plain CollectionSum of /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholdingForExcessCalculation, i.e. a sum of PER-W-2-ROW capped amounts, and the employer-EIN term disclosed the defect that left: an employer that issues one filer two Forms W-2 — which the W-2 instructions say in printed text it may do — can split an over-collection across them, each row stays under $10,918.20 on its own, nothing is capped, and the filer claims money the instruction routes to the employer and to Form 843. The row sum is still the MINUEND, because the total of a filer's group totals is the total of their rows; what is new is the SUBTRAHEND, /primaryFilerEmployerGroupDisallowedWithholding, which is the same filer's disallowed over-collection counted ONCE PER EMPLOYER. Subtracting it turns a sum of min(row, ceiling) into a sum of min(group, ceiling), which is what the printed rule adds. That fact carries the engine-capability argument and the S - ceiling x G construction; this one carries only the arithmetic.
NOTHING MOVES ON A RETURN WHOSE EMPLOYERS EACH ISSUED ONE FORM, which is every committed scenario and every conformance case: a one-W-2 group's capped total can never exceed the ceiling, so the subtrahend is $0 and this fact reproduces its prior value exactly.
THE ROUNDING CALL THIS UNIT WAS HANDED, DECIDED AND RECORDED. formW2s: /primaryFilerTotalOasdiWithholding is the additive first half of this credit, and its own Description names the open choice: it sums the WHOLE-DOLLAR item fact /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholding, so N W-2s contribute N separately rounded addends, which is the shape of the wage twin but not the shape of the i1040gi page 23 rule. THE DECISION IS CENTS-PRESERVING, ROUND ONCE AT LINE 11, on three grounds, and the first is dispositive on its own: (a) the printed rule governs this exact situation — "If you have to add two or more amounts to figure the amount to enter on a line, include cents when adding the amounts and round off only the total" — and Schedule 3 line 11 is such a line, adding N box-4 amounts and subtracting the cents-bearing $10,918.20; (b) this same pattern was already fixed the same way elsewhere in the withholding chain, and formW2s: /socialSecurityTaxesWithheld is the precedent — it sums the cents-bearing addends and rounds once; (c) the divergence is real and measured, not theoretical: the landed formW2s fixture w2-per-filer-oasdi-withholding-primary-two-employers pins 13,950 (per-item) against 13,951 (cents-preserving).
CONSEQUENCE, STATED PLAINLY RATHER THAN LEFT TO BE DISCOVERED: this unit therefore does NOT consume /{primary,secondary}FilerTotalOasdiWithholding. Two independent reasons, and the second is the stronger one — that pair also sums UNCAPPED box 4, so it could not have been the input to a correct line 11 whatever the rounding decision had been (see /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholdingForExcessCalculation on the per-employer cap). The pair stays exported and is now consumed by nothing; repointing it at the cents-preserving sibling or retiring it is a formW2s unit, outside this module's boundary. It is RECORDED here and in dictionary/ty2025/SOURCES.md rather than done silently; no issue is opened for it by this unit, so do not read this paragraph as a filing.

Fact.Name: Primary filer's excess social security tax withheld
Fact.Description:
The primary filer's own leg of Schedule 3 line 11: the capped box-4 total above the annual maximum, floored at zero, and ZERO unless the filer passes the eligibility test the instruction prints.
THE GATE IS THE INSTRUCTION'S OWN TEST, TERM FOR TERM, AND IT IS THE SECOND FALSE-ALLOWANCE GUARD. "If you, or your spouse if filing a joint return, had more than one employer for 2025 and total wages of more than $176,100, too much social security or tier 1 railroad retirement (RRTA) tax may have been withheld." [CORRECTED JUSTIFICATION — the prior example here (two employers at 88,050/5,600 each, "the 281.80 above the annual maximum is employer over-collection") described a W-2 the box-4 rate validation now proves impossible: with box 4 consistent against boxes 3+7, total withholding IS 6.2% of the wage total and nothing sits above the maximum at the base. The gate's real work is different: TIPS sit in the box-4 tax base (boxes 3+7) but NOT in the box-3-side eligibility measure, so the excess the gate holds back below the wage boundary is lawful tax on tips, not employer over-collection. The re-based denies witness pins a filer who paid 11,228.20 against the 10,918.20 maximum and receives 0 — held by this gate because the eligibility total reads exactly 176,100, not more.]
THE ELIGIBILITY MEASURE READS BOXES 3 PLUS 7: THE SHIPPING BOX-3-SIDE MEASURE WAS A KNOWN FALSE DENIAL. The two printed sentences this argument set against each other never conflicted, and that framing was the error. The Schedule 3 line 11 test says "total wages", not "box 3"; the W-2 instructions then define what the social security wage base IS, in three separate printed places, and all three say boxes 3 AND 7: (1) Box 5 states the identity outright — "The wages and tips subject to Medicare tax are the same as those subject to social security tax (boxes 3 and 7) except that there is no wage base limit for Medicare tax" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/iw2w3--2025.pdf, page 18, right column). (2) Box 3 defines itself by EXCLUSION from that base — "Show the total wages paid (before payroll deductions) subject to employee social security tax but not including social security tips and allocated tips" (same file, lines 1217-1220, left column). Box 3 is therefore the base MINUS tips by printed definition, never the base itself. (3) The cap is printed on the PAIR, twice — "The total of boxes 3 and 7 cannot exceed $176,100 (2025 maximum social security wage base)" (lines 1230-1232, left column, inside the Box 3 instruction) and "The total of boxes 3 and 7 should not be more than $176,100 (the maximum social security wage base for 2025)" (lines 1254-1259, right column, inside the Box 7 instruction). The wage base the line 11 threshold names is a bound on boxes 3 plus 7, so the quantity compared to it must be boxes 3 plus 7. A THIRD printed formulation agrees and reaches for an economic phrase rather than any box: "you will have excess social security or tier 1 railroad retirement tax withholding for 2025 only if your wages and compensation from two or more employers are more than $176,100" (https://www.irs.gov/pub/irs-prior/p505--2025.pdf, page 23). NO printed source anywhere in this repo's vendored set says box 3. Every formulation names the base. The coherence check settles it: box 4 is tax on boxes 3 plus 7 by its own instruction ("including social security tax on tips"), so measuring eligibility on box 3 alone compares a withholding total taken over one base against a threshold taken over a smaller one. That mismatch is exactly the 310.00 the re-based denies witness holds back, and it is lawful tax the filer paid.
THAT FINDING IS BUILT: the box-7 addend ships, and the paragraph at the end of this Description states what it moved. NOT VERIFIED, and named rather than implied: the statutory route through IRC section 3121 (tips as wages) and section 6413(c) (the special refund itself) would settle this from the law rather than from the instructions, and NEITHER is vendored in sources/ — usc26-3121 and usc26-6413 are both absent, so no subdivision of either is cited here (invariant #3). The printed instructions are sufficient on their own and are what this verdict rests on. tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-wage-base-boundary-{denies,allows} pins the boundary at exactly that dollar: 176,100 denies, 176,101 allows, because the printed test is a strict "more than".
THE GATE'S WAGE MEASURE IS WIDENED, and the paragraph above used to name a different fact. It said "formW2s:/primaryFilerExceedsMaxOasdiWages IS that test already — more than one W-2 AND the sum of the per-W-2 min(box 3, 176,100) above 176,100 — which is why the contract said the algebra of this credit was already in the graph under a different name." That was true of the SOCIAL SECURITY half and false of the tier-1 half the line's own title names, and the difference is not a detail: the W-2 instructions say of boxes 3 through 7 that "These boxes are not to be used to report railroad retirement compensation and taxes", so a railroad employee's box 3 is EMPTY and that gate reads $0 for them however much tier-1 tax was withheld. The gate is now /primaryFilerExceedsMaxOasdiOrTier1Wages, whose wage term adds each W-2's box-14 RRTA compensation before the per-employer cap. THE WAGE TERM alone was a strict superset, so no filer the old gate allowed was denied BY IT — but that sentence must not be read as a claim about the gate as a whole any more: the employer-EIN conjunct added later the same day narrows it deliberately (see /primaryFilerHasMoreThanOneEmployerEin, and the relation stated in both directions on /primaryFilerExceedsMaxOasdiOrTier1Wages). Meanwhile formW2s:/primaryFilerExceedsMaxOasdiWages is untouched and keeps its other consumer (the OASDI knockout chain through imported:/knockoutFormW2s) — see /formW2s/*/oasdiAndTier1WagesForExcessEligibility for why that chain was left alone.
THE "MORE THAN ONE EMPLOYER" HALF IS NOT REDUNDANT WITH THE CAP, AND IS NOW THE TERM THAT DOES THE WORK. The paragraph this replaces said it "nearly is" redundant: "With the per-employer cap in place a single-employer filer can never show more than 10,918.20 and so can never have a positive excess, so the count term changes no outcome by itself; it is carried because it is half of the printed test." The premise is that one employer means one capped row, and it fails the moment one employer issues TWO W-2s — the cap is applied per row, so that filer CAN show 12,400.00. The gate now carries /primaryFilerHasMoreThanOneEmployerEin beside the row count, and on the tail review's own case (two W-2s, one EIN, 6,200.00 each) it is the ONLY term that denies: the wage half passes at 200,000 and the cap does not bind on either row. tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-same-employer-two-w2s-denies measures it at 1,482 -> 0.
COMPLETE-SAFE BY WRAPPER, NOT BY LUCK. The gate is Incomplete on a return whose W-2 section has not been entered, and a Switch with an Incomplete condition resolves Incomplete — which would have carried up through Schedule 3 line 15 to Form 1040 line 31. The IsComplete conjunct in the first Case is what stops it; without it /otherPaymentsAndRefundableCreditsTotal turns from Complete to Placeholder. It is PINNED, not left to the corpus: tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-w2-section-absent-complete-safe removes the /formW2s collection entirely (absent, not empty — an empty collection makes the gate Complete-false and exercises nothing) and asserts both gates Placeholder against line 11 and Schedule 3 line 15 Complete at $0. Deleting the wrapper turns that case red. THE WIDENING KEEPS THE WRAPPER AND THE SHAPE: /primaryFilerExceedsMaxOasdiOrTier1Wages reads the same CollectionSize and CollectionSum over the same collection, so it is Incomplete in exactly the same circumstances, and that test was re-run against the new operand rather than assumed to still hold.
(a) An employer that over-withholds box 4 (or box-14 Tier 1) by LESS than the annual maximum, on a filer who also passes the wage gate, still inflates this leg dollar for dollar — the false-allowance direction. Closing it needs a per-W-2 withholding-against-6.2%-of-wages validation, which belongs in formW2s, not here. ⚠ THE FICA HALF OF (a) IS DISCHARGED, and the discharge happened in formW2s WITHOUT THIS PARAGRAPH BEING MOVED: the FICA-side validation needed here was already built elsewhere by the time this paragraph was checked. the per-W-2 fact formW2s:/formW2s/*/hasOasdiWithholdingAboveRateOnOasdiWagesAndTips is exactly the validation this sentence asks for: it bounds each W-2's box 4 at 6.2% of LesserOf(box 3 + box 7, the wage base), and it is wired into formW2s:/hasW2ValidationErrors, which carries BlockSubmissionOnTrue. So the return this residual describes can no longer be FILED. Two things that discharge does NOT do, both stated because the difference is the whole of what survives: it REFUSES rather than recomputes — no corrected box 4 is inferred, and the filer is sent back to the employer and to Form 843, which is where the printed instruction sends them — and it cannot reach the BOX-14 TIER 1 half, because Form W-2 reports no tier-1 wage base to take 6.2% of. The tier-1 half of (a) is therefore the whole of what is left of it, and it is bounded by the same absence residual (b) names. The node test tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-residual-a-overwithholding-blocked-by-w2-validation measures the FICA half end to end: 1,900.00 of phantom credit on a two-employer return, with the validation true beside it. That case asserts the inflated figure as a MEASUREMENT of the residue, not as intent, and it inverts by construction if a later unit ever recomputes instead of refusing. The OTHER half of that residual — a W-2 with box 3 AND box 4 both absent — cannot reach this fact: with no withholding there is nothing to claim, so the gate reading zero denies a credit that is zero anyway. (b) The tier-1 wage measure's own residual, stated in full on /formW2s/*/oasdiAndTier1WagesForExcessEligibility: box-14 "RRTA compensation" is total (Medicare-equivalent) compensation and the tier-1 base can be smaller, so the gate can open on compensation the tier-1 base would not reach. No separate tier-1 base is reported on Form W-2. (c) THE W-2-ROW-versus-EMPLOYER CONFLATION, found by the tail review, HALF CLOSED AND HALF STILL OPEN. It read: "every term of this surface keys on W-2 ROWS, not on EMPLOYERS — 'more than one employer' is a CollectionSize over W-2s, and the $10,918.20 disallowance caps each W-2 separately." BOTH HALVES WERE TRUE. The COUNT half is now fixed: the gate carries /primaryFilerHasMoreThanOneEmployerEin beside the row count, so W-2s sharing one box-b EIN no longer satisfy "more than one employer," and the tail review's own witness — two W-2s, one employer, 6,200.00 of box 4 each — moves from a claimed 1,482 to 0, which is where the printed rule puts it ("The employer should adjust the tax for you. If the employer doesn't adjust the overcollection, you can file a claim for refund using Form 843"). tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-same-employer-two-w2s-denies is that case, and it was RED before the term landed.
RESIDUAL (c) IS CLOSED. THE PARAGRAPH THAT STOOD HERE CLAIMED IT COULD NOT BE. What it said: "the per-employer CAP is still applied per W-2 ROW. A filer with TWO OR MORE distinct employers, one of which splits an over-collection across several of its own W-2s, still claims that employer's excess" — direction false-allowance, witnessed at 7,682 against a printed 6,200 on the fixture it filed as excess-oasdi-split-employer-group-cap-RESIDUAL. That is fixed: /primaryFilerTotalOasdiWithholdingForExcess now subtracts /primaryFilerEmployerGroupDisallowedWithholding, the ceiling binds the employer GROUP, and that same fixture — renamed -exact — resolves 6,200.
WHY THE OLD CAPABILITY ARGUMENT WAS WRONG, kept rather than deleted because it is the kind of claim that must be corrected in the open. It ran: the fix needs min(group withholding, $10,918.20) SUMMED ONCE PER GROUP; the per-row group SUM is expressible via CollectionSum(Switch(sibling key equals ../key -> sibling amount, else $0)); but ATTRIBUTING it once per group is not, because summing a symmetric per-row value multiplies each group by its size and correcting for the size needs either an exact division (Dollar is a BigDecimal at Scale = 2, HALF_EVEN) or a designated first-of-group, which needs an order the engine does not have. EVERY STEP OF THAT IS STILL TRUE, and the group SUM half was verified working before a line of this unit was written. The error was the last step: the conclusion assumed ATTRIBUTION is the only route from per-row facts to a per-group figure. It is not. Where at most ONE group busts the ceiling, every other row's disallowance is $0 and the over-cap group's rows all carry the same figure, so MAXIMUM over the rows IS that figure — exactly, in integer cents, attributing nothing, dividing nothing, ordering nothing. Maximum is an Expression.Aggregate exactly as Count and CollectionSum are (Maximum.scala, Count.scala, CollectionSum.scala), and "at most one group is over" is itself decided exactly by a pigeonhole on two row counts (/primaryFilerHasAtMostOneOverCapEmployer). TWO SMALLER CORRECTIONS TO THAT PARAGRAPH'S ENGINE READING, neither of which changes its verdict: IndexOf does NOT take a literal Int — IndexOf.scala's apply takes an IntNode and fromDerivedConfig accepts any IntNode child, so a derived index is legal; it is still useless here because a member fact cannot obtain its OWN index. And the reason division is dead is stronger than "Dollar rounds": there is no Dollar-to-Rational node at all, so the exact-rational escape (Rational is a first-class type with its own CollectionSum operator) cannot be entered from a Dollar, and both Divide(Dollar, Int) and Multiply(Dollar, Rational) round through Fractional[Dollar].div at scale 2.
WHAT SURVIVES IS NARROWER AND POINTS THE OTHER WAY — a bounded false DENIAL, not a false allowance. Where TWO OR MORE of ONE filer's employers each over-collected in the same year, neither the maximum nor any expressible sum gives the printed answer, and /primaryFilerEmployerGroupDisallowedWithholding deliberately takes the branch that over-states the disallowance. tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-two-over-cap-employers-exact is that filer — two employers, two W-2s each at 6,200.00 — and asserts the 7,954.60 this dictionary computes with the printed 10,918.20 derived beside it in the transcript, so the gap is a pinned quantity rather than a paragraph. THE EXIT is unchanged in kind and now smaller in scope: an engine unit under adding an aggregate-by-key primitive, which would collapse all three branches to one; or the /employers data-model reshape, which also fixes residual (a) for free and remains a formW2s.xml change plus an intake and a stored- return migration.
BOUNDED, RE-DERIVED FOR THIS UNIT RATHER THAN INHERITED: of 1,906 fixture and scenario documents in the repository's tests and scenarios, 238 carry two or more W-2 rows and exactly FOUR carry two rows sharing BOTH a filer and the full employer key — all four are this surface's own node tests. No scenario and no conformance case is among them, so this correction moves no corpus row. (The earlier "229 multi-W-2 fixtures" count in this paragraph was the same scan taken a day earlier and before this unit's fixtures landed.) The corpus does carry same-EIN pairs — scenarios/upstream/mfj-30k.json and scenarios/units/u057/* — but always one W-2 per SPOUSE, which sections 3101/3201 make two separate situations and which the per-filer grouping correctly leaves alone.
THE PER-W-2 WAGE MEASURE ADDS the complete-safe box-7 tip fact inside the existing LesserOf, alongside box 3 and box-14 RRTA compensation. The existing `/writableOasdiTips` input, complete-safe `/oasdiTipsUnrounded` fact and `/oasdiTips` MeF export already form the route, so no intake or screen change was needed. The formerly false-denial tipped witness `excess-oasdi-wage-base-boundary-denies` now asserts the Schedule 3 wage total and eligibility gate at $181,100 and the resulting $310 credit. `excess-oasdi-box7-tips-cross-eligibility` establishes a near-cap $177,000 total and $55.80 credit; `excess-oasdi-no-tips-control` leaves box 7 unanswered at the exact $176,100 boundary and keeps the strict gate closed. All three cases include hand derivations.

Fact.Name: Schedule 3 line 11 — excess social security and tier 1 RRTA tax withheld
Fact.Description:
Schedule 3 (Form 1040) line 11, "Excess social security and tier 1 RRTA tax withheld" — the two per-filer legs added and rounded ONCE to whole dollars. Feeds Schedule 3 line 15 (/otherPaymentsAndRefundableCreditsTotal) and through it Form 1040 line 31, and is read by ctcOdc:/socialSecurityOverEitc as the Schedule 8812 line-24 term.
Its coupled half retires formW2s:/anyFilerExceedsMaxOasdiWages from flow:/flowIsKnockedOut. Until this commit, every return that would claim this credit was refused at submission, so the credit and the refusal could not be separated: building the credit alone produced a fact no filed return could reach, and retiring the refusal alone would have let an over-cap filer file with the credit silently omitted.
WHAT THE FILL CORRECTS DOWNSTREAM, and this was the research finding the unit was asked to verify: ctcOdc:/socialSecurityOverEitc (Schedule 8812 line 25 = line 23 - line 24) subtracted only the EITC, because Schedule 3 line 11 — the OTHER component of line 24 — did not exist. Line 24 is SUBTRACTED, so the omission OVER-stated line 25 and could OVER-claim the Part II-B additional child tax credit: a false allowance, and the confirmed one. It is now wired. tests/nodes/ty2025/ctcOdc/sched8812-line24-excess-oasdi-leg witnesses the movement on a two-employer return (line 25 falls from 15,300 to 13,818).
THE CORRECTION IS A RENDERED-LINE CORRECTION ON EVERY CURRENTLY REPRESENTABLE RETURN, stated that way because the stronger claim would be false. Line 26 is the LARGER of line 20 (15% of earned income over 2,500) and line 25, and any filer who can reach a positive line 11 has social security wages above 176,100 — at which point line 20 is over 26,000 while line 25 is of the order of the filer's own FICA withholding, so line 26 takes line 20 and /maximumActc does not move. The line-26 dominance argument is ANALYTIC, not witnessed: the witness test asserts line 21, line 11 and line 25, and its fixture has no qualifying children, so /maximumActc is $0 on both sides of the change and could not show the flatness either way. The same disclosure shape was used for the line-21 correction, with the weaker evidence named rather than implied.
WHOLE DOLLARS, ROUNDED HERE AND NOWHERE UPSTREAM: the two legs carry cents all the way in, per i1040gi page 23 — see /primaryFilerTotalOasdiWithholdingForExcess for the decision and why the shipped formW2s per-filer withholding pair is not the input.
TIER 1 RRTA IS MODELED, and the paragraph this replaces is kept in the next sentence because the correction is the record. IT READ: "TIER 1 RRTA IS NOT MODELED and this fact must not be read as covering it. The line's own title names tier 1 RRTA tax, and a railroad employer reports Tier 1 in box 14 rather than box 4, so this computation sees none of it." The diagnosis was exactly right, and this build reflects it. Both terms of the credit now carry the tier-1 half: /formW2s/*/oasdiWithholdingForExcessCalculation adds each W-2's box-14 Tier 1 tax to its box 4 inside the per-employer cap (one pool, one $10,918.20 ceiling — "social security and/or Tier 1 RRTA tax withheld"), and the eligibility gate is /{primary,secondary}FilerExceedsMaxOasdiOrTier1Wages, whose wage measure adds box-14 RRTA compensation because boxes 3 through 7 "are not to be used to report railroad retirement compensation and taxes". Witnessed by tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-tier1-two-railroad-employers (a two-railroad- employer filer moves from $0 to $1,482 — the taxpayer-ADVERSE omission the retirement contract named as blocker (i)) and excess-oasdi-tier1-mixed-fica-and-railroad-one-pool (the combined pool).
IT IS STILL UNREACHABLE ON A FILED RETURN, and that is intended rather than a defect. Both box-14 RRTA submission knockouts remain armed — formW2s:/hasABox14NYRRTAValueWeKnockout and /flowKnockoutHasRRTACodesInBox14NotInNY, the latter WIDENED — so every return that can reach a positive tier-1 leg is refused at submission. Each of the four tier-1 node tests asserts that refusal firing beside the credit it computes. Retiring the knockouts is separate work; this fact is its prerequisite.
TIER 2 RRTA is not claimable on Form 1040 at all ("You can't claim a refund for excess tier 2 RRTA tax on Form 1040, 1040-SR, or 1040-NR. Instead, use Form 843"), so its absence is correct rather than a gap, and nothing is built for it. Pinned rather than merely asserted: tests/nodes/ty2025/schedule3/excess-oasdi-tier1-tier2-excluded reports 9,800.00 of Tier 2 and line 11 does not move.

Amount from Schedule 3, line 15 (line 31 1040).
THE LINE-11 TERM is /excessSocialSecurityTaxWithheld, excess social security and tier 1 RRTA tax withheld. It is $0 for every filer who did not exhaust the social security wage base with more than one employer, so no return that could already file moves — but it is NOT merely additive in the safe sense, because the same fill retires the knockout that refused the returns on which it is positive. Those returns become computable for the first time; see flow.xml at the removal site.
THE LINE-12 AND LINE-14 TERMS: /sched3Line12 (credit for federal tax on fuels, the round 35 intake) and /sched3Line14 (total other payments or refundable credits, lines 13a through 13z). Both complete-safe 0 and $0 on every committed scenario, so this is additive in the safe sense: no prior return moves. With them the printed "Add lines 9 through 12 and 14" is the whole sum.
